title: Regional regressions
text:
Per country \text{BF-NEE} = R^{crop} \sum_c S_c P_c + R^{past} P^{past} = R \cdot w, with the effective attribution weight w = \text{BF-NEE}/R (cropland and pasture part combined). A log-log model

\log(\text{BF-NEE}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \log(R) + \beta_2 \log(w) + \varepsilon

has \beta_1 = \beta_2 = 1 and R^2 = 1 by construction. Deviations therefore point to data problems – not to substantive effects. The model serves as a consistency check; the interesting part is how much each component varies between regions.
Only countries with BF-NEE > 0 are used (log scale); regions need ≥ 6 observations.

title: Interactive map
text:
Choose a period, an ecosystem group and a commodity. The map shows either the agriculture-constrained natural ecosystem loss or the BF-NEE (loss × attribution weight of the producing country). Hover over a cell for its value; select a country to zoom in and see its totals.







About the map data





Cells are aggregated for the web (about 18 km); values are km² per displayed cell. Totals in the side panel come from the country tables, not from the display raster. The map data are built on the cluster with data-raw/02_build_map_data.R and uploaded with shiny/global_map/deploy.R.

title: Natural ecosystem loss behind consumption
text:
BF-NEE links the loss of natural ecosystems through agricultural expansion to the commodities grown on the new land and to final demand – here, consumption in Germany. Results are available for every producing country, time period, commodity and ecosystem type.

section: What is new in this version
text:
What is new in this version






v3 (data built 2026-10-26 14:34 CET)

Intensive pasture (v3). Cropland and intensive pasture count as agricultural land. Loss linked to pasture expansion is attributed to grazing livestock.
Commodity shares from expansion. A crop’s share is now its increase in area relative to the total increase of all expanding crops in the same period. Crops whose area shrank get a share of zero.
Agricultural-expansion constraint. Only natural ecosystem loss that coincides with agricultural expansion in the same grid cell is attributed (Eq. 31–32).
Ecosystem classes are kept. The constrained loss is split back onto the ecosystem classes in proportion to their original loss, so footprints by ecosystem type add up exactly to the total footprint.

title: Countries
text:
What drives a country’s footprint?
BF-NEE of a country is its agriculture-constrained loss multiplied by its attribution weight \sum_c S_c P_c. Countries can rank high because they lose a lot of ecosystems, because a large share of their expanding crops ends up in German final demand – or both.

title: Method
text:
BF-NEE combines three data sets that each play a distinct role:







Data set
Role




LandSHIFT
Cropland extent per grid cell; crop composition per country


GlobES
Composition of ecosystem classes (IUCN habitat scheme) and its change


GLORIA (MRIO)
Share of each crop’s production that ends up in German final demand



The analysis covers the years 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010 and 2015 and therefore four five-year periods. Each period y-1 \rightarrow y is combined with the commodity and GLORIA factors of its end year y.

title: Method
text:
BF-NEE combines three data sets that each play a distinct role:







Data set
Role




LandSHIFT
Cropland extent per grid cell; crop composition per country


GlobES
Composition of ecosystem classes (IUCN habitat scheme) and its change


GLORIA (MRIO)
Share of each crop’s production that ends up in German final demand



The analysis covers the years 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010 and 2015 and therefore four five-year periods. Each period y-1 \rightarrow y is combined with the commodity and GLORIA factors of its end year y.

title: Method
text:
1 · Harmonising cropland
LandSHIFT is the authoritative source for cropland. In every grid cell the GlobES agricultural classes (14.1 arable land, 15.8 seasonally flooded agricultural land) are rescaled to the LandSHIFT cropland fraction L_{p,y}, and all other classes are rescaled so that the cell still sums to one. Six anthropogenic classes (14.4, 14.5, 15.4, 15.5, 15.6, 15.11) are removed beforehand.


\sum_{a \in A} G'_{p,a,y} = L_{p,y}, \qquad \sum_e G'_{p,e,y} = 1, \qquad
A_{p,e,y} = G'_{p,e,y}\,A_p

title: Method
text:
1b · Intensive pasture






Since v3. Intensive pasture is part of the agricultural land.



LandSHIFT assigns a grazing fraction to every cell with livestock, both intensive pastures and extensive grazing on natural vegetation such as savanna. LandSHIFT separates the two only by stocking density, using the country mean as the threshold. BF-NEE follows this with one fixed threshold per country: the mean stocking density of the grazing land in 1995–2015, weighted by grazing area. A cell’s grazing fraction counts as intensive pasture L^{past}_{p,y} if its stocking density is above that threshold. Extensive grazing stays part of the natural GlobES cover.
GlobES is coupled to both agricultural land uses separately:


\sum_{a \in \{14.1,\,15.8\}} G'_{p,a,y} = L^{crop}_{p,y}, \qquad
G'_{p,14.2,y} = L^{past}_{p,y}, \qquad
G'_{p,e,y} = \tilde G_{p,e,y}\,\frac{1 - L^{crop}_{p,y} - L^{past}_{p,y}}{1 - \tilde G^{crop}_{p,y} - \tilde G^{past}_{p,y}}


Pastureland (14.2) is therefore an agricultural class and no longer counted as natural.

title: Method
text:
2 · Loss of natural ecosystems
For every natural ecosystem class e the gross loss between two observations is


\text{Loss}_{p,e,y} = \max\!\left(-\Delta A_{p,e,y},\,0\right), \qquad
N_{p,y} = \sum_{e \in N} \text{Loss}_{p,e,y}


Expansion of one natural class does not offset the loss of another.

title: Method
text:
3 · Agricultural-expansion constraint
Not every ecosystem change is caused by agriculture. Only loss that coincides with a net increase of agricultural land (cropland + intensive pasture) in the same grid cell and period is attributed. Pasture converted to cropland is not counted as expansion:


\text{Gain}^{agri}_{p,y} = \max\!\left(\Delta A^{crop}_{p,y} + \Delta A^{past}_{p,y},\,0\right), \qquad
R_{p,y} = \min\!\left(N_{p,y},\ \text{Gain}^{agri}_{p,y}\right)


R is split in every cell into a cropland and a pasture part in proportion to the positive changes of the two land uses:


s^{past}_{p,y} = \frac{\max(\Delta A^{past}_{p,y},0)}{\max(\Delta A^{crop}_{p,y},0) + \max(\Delta A^{past}_{p,y},0)}, \qquad
R^{past}_{p,y} = s^{past}_{p,y} R_{p,y}, \quad R^{crop}_{p,y} = (1 - s^{past}_{p,y}) R_{p,y}

title: Method
Method
text:
5 · Commodity shares from expansion






Since v2. Previously the static share of each crop in total cropland was used.



Ecosystems are converted by crops that expand, not by fields that already exist. For each country and period, the share of crop c is its area increase relative to the summed increase of all expanding crops:


S_{c,r,y} =
\frac{\max\!\left(A_{c,r,y} - A_{c,r,y-1},\,0\right)}
     {\sum_{c'} \max\!\left(A_{c',r,y} - A_{c',r,y-1},\,0\right)}


Crops whose area shrank get S = 0; the shares of a period sum to one. If no crop expanded, all shares are zero and nothing is attributed.

title: Method
text:
6 · Attribution and indicator
The cropland part is attributed to crops with the commodity share and the GLORIA production share P_{c,r,y} (share of production in country r that is used for German final demand). The pasture part is attributed to Grazing livestock, whose P^{past} is the mean of the GLORIA sectors Raising of cattle and Raising of sheep and goats:


L_{p,e,c,y} = R^{crop}_{p,e,y}\,S_{c,r,y}\,P_{c,r,y}, \qquad
L_{p,e,past,y} = R^{past}_{p,e,y}\,P^{past}_{r,y}, \qquad
\text{BF-NEE}_y = \sum_p \sum_e \Big(\sum_c L_{p,e,c,y} + L_{p,e,past,y}\Big)


Summing L_{p,e,c,y} over any subset gives the footprint of that subset – e.g. of one ecosystem group, one country or one commodity. All values are areas in km².

title: Method
text:
Limitations

Commodity and GLORIA factors are national, not pixel-specific: the indicator does not identify the crop planted on a specific converted pixel.
The constraint is spatially conservative – loss is attributed only where cropland grows in the same cell and five-year period. Transitions that happen and reverse between snapshots are not captured.
Only intensive pasture is agricultural land; the split between intensive and extensive grazing depends on the country-mean threshold. Cattle and sheep/goats are weighted equally in P^{past} (no per-cell information on species).
The LandSHIFT–GLORIA concordance is not one-to-one (e.g. pulses and oil crops share one GLORIA sector).
